questions.q: What does Pulizzi advise new content marketers to do first?
a: Choose one platform and publish consistently
Join every social network at once
Buy ads on the biggest platforms
Hire a team of content creators
questions.why: Lesson 1 says focusing on a single channel helps you reach a big milestone much faster than spreading yourself thin.

questions.q: Why is an email subscriber more valuable than a social follower?
a: You own the list and control what reaches them
Email subscribers spend more money on average
Email is cheaper to run than social media
Subscribers share content far more often
questions.why: Lesson 2 explains that an email list is an asset you own, unlike a following on someone else's platform.

questions.q: What does the summary compare relying on social media to?
a: Building on land that belongs to someone else
Planting seeds in a rented garden
Renting a car instead of buying one
Borrowing a ladder to reach the roof
questions.why: Pulizzi warns that a social following sits on someone else's platform, so you should build assets you control.

questions.q: When should you expand to other channels?
a: Only after one channel is well established
As soon as you publish your first post
When you have fewer than 100 followers
Before you have picked a niche or audience
questions.why: Lesson 3 advises focus now and diversification later, once your main platform has grown strong.

questions.q: How did Mimi Ikonn build a large following across platforms?
a: By focusing on YouTube for years before diversifying
By posting the same content everywhere daily
By buying followers on Instagram
By running contests on Pinterest
questions.why: The summary says her other accounts were a splash from the wave made by her main YouTube channel.
